reviews.reason: The canvas keeps module-level ZoomToolbar, ViewportObserver, PendingLocateNodeEffect, inner canvas and provider wrapper as one UI owner with stable component types. Element projection, action refs and ReactFlow node/edge synchronization are extracted into useAgentFlowCanvasElements. The three existing helper component bodies are byte-identical to the reviewed source before fc16a5c71; the extraction introduces no render-local component definitions or helper remounts.

ViewportObserver observes the external ReactFlow provider viewport and sends x/y/zoom snapshots to existing parent refs used by save/restore. Its effect depends on those three viewport primitives and the callback; it does not create a second parent state owner. Getter registration and cleanup remain separate, and the fc16a5c71 extraction leaves all observer effects byte-identical.

ViewportObserver registers the mounted ReactFlow provider viewport getter and unregisters it with null during cleanup. Existing AgentFlow and Workflow consumers write that getter into refs used by save/restore; the effect does not mirror local child state into parent state. Its dependencies remain the getter callback and provider instance. The fc16a5c71 extraction leaves this observer body byte-identical.

This existing handler is a live controller callback, not a component type. It updates selectedVariable only when key matches and invokes debugSession.setVariableCacheValue; no child effect or memo compares this callback to own a native lifetime. AgentFlowCanvasFrame retains editor UI composition and draft/session orchestration; useCanvasDockLayout owns all dock state/ResizeObserver/resize cleanup, and useCanvasNodePreview owns missing-variable planning and run receipts. The export mutation only reads a generated archive and saves it locally; it does not change backend catalog data. P21b reassessed 2026-11-17: Canvas changes add run locking, stable action refs and functional node/edge synchronization while retaining module-level ViewportObserver registration/cleanup and x/y/zoom notification. Frame and Workflow witnesses now consume backend analysis and fence running interactions; canvas interaction tests retain readable selection and assert graph writes stay blocked during a run. Separate dock and preview hooks retain resource ownership. P21c stabilizes omitted assembly defaults after proving downstream identity consumers; that default-value tuple stays held. The public flow-editor facade remains the kernel boundary. Environment/conversation panels still own editable commit/cancel drafts, and current resize handles include keyboard callbacks and orientation/value semantics.
